papers_read.title_as_printed: Plasma p-tau217 identifies cognitively normal older adults who will develop cognitive impairment in a 10-year window
papers_read.note: Yakoub Y, Gonzalez-Ortiz F, Ashton NJ, et al., Villeneuve S. Alzheimer's Dement. 2025;21:e14537, doi 10.1002/alz.14537.

papers_read.title_as_printed: Blood biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease and progression across different stages of cognitive decline in the community
papers_read.note: Valletta M, Vetrano DL, Gregorio C, et al., Grande G. Nature Communications (2025) 16:10412, doi 10.1038/s41467-025-66728-2.

what_each_reports.P-1403: Cohort: PREVENT-AD, cognitively unimpaired adults with a first-degree family history of AD (plasma sample n=215; mean age 65.2 at classification; 73% female; 41% APOE e4 carriers). Follow-up: mean 5.65 years after plasma (range 1.01-10.47). MCI was classified by blinded consensus. Plasma A/T groups used Abeta42/40 < 0.09 (IP-MS) and p-tau217 > 3.98 pg/mL (in-house Simoa; 2 SD above the mean of Abeta-PET-negative CU adults). Group sizes: A+T+ 21 (16 progressed), A-T+ 7 (5), A+T- 60 (14), A-T- 127 (25). Cox models vs A-T-: A+T+ HR 7.81 (95% CI 3.92-15.59), P<0.001; A-T+ HR 4.25 (1.60-11.31), P=0.004; A+T- HR 1.14 (0.58-2.24), P=0.69. Continuous-biomarker ROC AUCs across plasma, CSF and PET: 0.74-0.81 for tau, 0.77-0.82 for Abeta+tau. The authors say the HRs should be interpreted with caution (small A+T+ and A-T+ groups; 20% of A-T- progressed).
what_each_reports.P-1421: Cohort: SNAC-K, a random population sample aged 60+ from Stockholm, with 2148 dementia-free participants followed (median age 72.2; 61.5% female; 381 with MCI at baseline). Follow-up: mean 9.6 years, up to 16. Markers were measured in serum by Simoa (ALZpath p-tau217). Analysis used multistate Markov models on an age time scale. NC to MCI: p-tau217 high vs low (cut-off 0.134 pg/mL, the Youden optimum for 10-year all-cause dementia; 803 vs 1345 participants) HR 1.07 (0.73-1.56) basic and 1.19 (0.75-1.88) fully adjusted. Abeta42/40 low vs high HR 0.98 (0.72-1.34). None of the six markers was associated with NC to MCI, whether as continuous splines, as dichotomies, or as combinations of p-tau217, NfL and GFAP. The same markers did predict MCI to AD dementia: p-tau217 HR 2.11 (1.61-2.76); NfL 2.34 (1.77-3.11); three elevated markers 3.71 (2.22-6.20).

quantity_a: Hazard of incident all-cause MCI in CU adults with a first-degree family history of AD, as a Cox HR over a mean 5.65 years after plasma sampling. MCI: blinded consensus requiring more than 1.0 SD below norms on an RBANS composite or two RAVLT scores, plus a subjective memory complaint and/or observed decline. Exposure: joint plasma A+T+ (or A-T+) status vs A-T-, with thresholds anchored to Abeta-PET-negative CU adults.
quantity_b: Hazard of the NC-to-MCI transition in a random community sample aged 60+, as a multistate Markov HR on an age time scale over a mean 9.6 years (up to 16). MCI: psychometric, 1.5 SD or more below the age-specific mean in at least one of five domains with preserved function; reversion allowed. Exposure: single serum markers above vs below Youden cut-offs derived for 10-year all-cause dementia (p-tau217 > 0.134 pg/mL; 37% of participants 'high'), plus continuous splines.
incompatible_if_same: On the tau arm, yes. P-1403's A+T+ interval (3.92-15.59) and P-1421's p-tau217 interval (0.73-1.56 basic; 0.75-1.88 fully adjusted) exclude each other. P-1403's A-T+ lower bound (1.60) lies just above P-1421's basic upper bound (1.56) but inside its fully adjusted interval. On the amyloid arm, no. P-1403's A+T- vs A-T- HR 1.14 (0.58-2.24) and P-1421's Abeta42/40 HR 0.98 (0.72-1.34) are both null and overlap. The candidate therefore stands or falls on whether the tau-arm quantities are the same, and they are not.

gates.task: match: both are T2 prognosis, and the contested arm is incident MCI from normal cognition in both. P-1421's registry substage MCI_to_AD describes its headline result, but it also reports the NC-to-MCI transition.
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: PREVENT-AD (Montreal; a research cohort enriched for family history) vs SNAC-K (Stockholm; population-based). No waiver on the record.
gates.validation_tier: n/a: both are association studies that validate no model (registry V2 for both); counted as matched.
gates.modality_family: match: fluid (blood) biomarkers. The subtype differs: plasma (in-house Gothenburg Simoa p-tau217, IP-MS Abeta42/40) vs serum (ALZpath Simoa p-tau217, Simoa Neuro 3-plex A Abeta42/40).

endpoint_and_metric: The metric is compatible (hazard ratios in both); the endpoint is shared in name only. 'MCI' is defined differently: consensus with a complaint or decline requirement vs a single-visit psychometric criterion with modelled reversion. Follow-up differs (mean 5.65 vs 9.6 years). The exposures differ: joint A/T status on AD-anchored cut-offs vs single-marker dichotomies on dementia-optimised cut-offs.
performance_validity: Not a performance comparison (hazard-ratio associations). Neither paper is flagged, and P-1403's AUCs (0.66-0.82) are far below the 0.97 test.
independence: Independent: different cohorts, countries and author teams, with no shared authors or participants.
grounds: The exposure contrasts differ. P-1403's HR of 7.81 compares joint plasma A+T+ with A-T-, on thresholds anchored to Abeta-PET-negative CU adults; A+T+ is 10% of its sample (p.3, p.4). P-1421's HR of 1.07 compares serum p-tau217 above vs below a cut-off tuned to predict 10-year all-cause dementia, with 803 of 2148 participants 'high' (p.4, p.6). P-1421 has no A/T classification. P-1403 reports no whole-sample single-marker or continuous hazard ratio: its Cox models are by A/T group only, and its continuous analysis is ROC AUC (p.4, p.8).

The population behind the 'cognitively unimpaired older adults' label differs. PREVENT-AD enrols only people with a first-degree family history of AD (p.3). SNAC-K is a random community sample aged 60+ with median age 72.2, 865 of 2148 aged 78 or over (p.2, p.6). Both papers note that MCI can arise without AD pathology: P-1403 says most A-T- progressors probably have non-neurodegenerative conditions (p.10), and P-1421 says mild cognitive deficits are not necessarily the expression of an underlying neuropathology (p.5). P-1403 also names community settings as untested (p.3).
The dataset-family gate fails (PREVENT-AD vs SNAC-K) and no waiver is on the record. Under the C-232 precedent, waiving the cohort gate would not cure an exposure (predictor) mismatch.

The endpoint and horizon differ. P-1403 counts consensus MCI requiring a subjective complaint and/or observed decline, over a mean 5.65 years after plasma (p.4). P-1421 counts psychometric MCI (1.5 SD or more below the age-specific mean in one domain) with reversion modelled, over a mean 9.6 years (p.2, p.6).
Matrix and assay differ: plasma on an in-house Gothenburg Simoa vs serum on the ALZpath Simoa. P-1421 states that its cohort-derived cut-offs may not carry over to other laboratory platforms (p.6).

On the closest shared quantity, amyloid alone, the two agree: both are null (P-1403 p.7; P-1421 Table 2, p.4). Including Abeta42/40 in the record's disagreement therefore adds no disagreement. The tension is confined to the tau arm, where the exposures differ.

In fairness to the candidate: P-1421's null also holds for continuous p-tau217 (splines, p.2), so the tension is not only a cut-off artefact, and the two papers' headline answers do diverge. It stays unadjudicable because no like-for-like hazard ratio exists across the two papers.

record_defects: conflict_statement's '62/228 progressors over a mean 5.65-year post-classification follow-up' mixes denominators. 62/228 is the whole study sample (P-1403 p.4), while 5.65 years is the plasma sample's follow-up. The plasma sample (n=215) had 60 progressors (16+14+5+25, p.5).

conflict_statement's 'combined biomarker AUC 0.77-0.82' is the range across the plasma, CSF and PET combined models (p.8), not a plasma-only figure. The plasma-specific AUC appears only in Figure 3, not in the text.

conflict_statement's 'plasma p-tau217-based A+T+ status' leaves out that A+T+ also requires plasma Abeta42/40 below 0.09 by IP-MS (p.3). The HR of 7.81 is a joint A/T contrast against A-T-, not a p-tau217 marker effect; the record's own review_note says the same.

conflict_statement's 'the same markers strongly predicted MCI-to-dementia (NfL HR 2.34, p-tau217 HR 2.11)' uses the hazard ratios for MCI to AD dementia. For all-cause dementia they are 1.84 and 1.74 (P-1421 p.2).

conflict_statement counts 'Abeta42/40 among them' as part of the disagreement, but P-1403's own amyloid-only contrast is also null (A+T- vs A-T- HR 1.14, 0.58-2.24; p.7). On amyloid the two papers agree.

conflict_type 'semantic_directional' overstates the pair. It is a strong positive association set against a null whose point estimates lie slightly above 1 (1.07 basic, 1.19 fully adjusted), not opposite directions.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Two things together: a waiver of the dataset-family gate on the record, and a like-for-like exposure. Examples: SNAC-K reporting NC-to-MCI hazards for an A+T+ vs A-T- classification or for an AD-anchored p-tau217 threshold; or PREVENT-AD reporting a whole-sample, single-marker p-tau217 hazard ratio at a comparable cut-off. The pair would become a genuine candidate if such a contrast still gave non-overlapping intervals and there were evidence that family-history enrichment does not change the share of incident MCI that is AD-driven. A SNAC-K NC-to-MCI estimate for participants under 78, closer in age to PREVENT-AD, would bear on the population ground; the main text does not give one.
